governanceNotes: D1 batch 61 (2026-09-26): six bounded association edges authored - multiple-endocrine-neoplasia to hyperparathyroidism (rank 1), to pituitary-neoplasm (rank 2), to pheochromocytoma (rank 3), to thyroid-cancer (rank 4), to gastrinoma (rank 5), and to insulinoma (rank 6) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The hyperparathyroidism proposition rests on the Russian 102-patient MEN1 cohort (PMID 41834593), the South Korea nationwide cohort (PMID 40607214), and the 14-study MEN2 review of 3,783 carriers (PMID 40277809). The pituitary proposition rests on the nationwide 240-patient MEN1 cohort (PMID 40921719), the Russian cohort (PMID 41834593), and the Korean cohort (PMID 40607214). The pheochromocytoma proposition rests on the 309-patient RET-genotype cohort (PMID 28605116), the MEN2 pheochromocytoma review (PMID 32388798), and the de novo MEN2A case (PMID 42272368). The thyroid-cancer proposition rests on the 309-patient cohort (PMID 28605116), the RET K666N family study (PMID 39963300), and the de novo case (PMID 42272368). The gastrinoma proposition rests on the AFCE-GTE surgical cohort (PMID 33649917), the MEN1 pregnancy case (PMID 33597314), and the Russian cohort (PMID 41834593). The insulinoma proposition rests on the 46-center international cohort (PMID 32352164), the AFCE-GTE cohort (PMID 33649917), and the Korean cohort (PMID 40607214).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) subtype heterogeneity - MEN1 (parathyroid, pituitary, pancreaticoduodenal) and MEN2 (medullary carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and a minority hyperparathyroidism) differ in mechanism and penetrance; each edge records its subtype scope and the pooled identity is used only at the catalog level; (ii) histotype scope - the thyroid-cancer edge is explicitly scoped to medullary thyroid carcinoma because the catalog lacks a medullary identity, and the pancreatic-cancer proposition was withheld as a semantic mismatch (neuroendocrine versus ductal); (iii) ascertainment limits - the Korean cohort is clinically suspected rather than genetically confirmed, surgical series are referral-conditioned, and screening intensity drives pituitary detection; (iv) genotype-phenotype limits - RET codon status drives wide penetrance variation (10-80 percent for pheochromocytoma) and the exon 10 pituitary signal is single-center; (v) intermediate-node discipline - hormone-consequence pathways (kidney stones, osteoporosis, hypertension, peptic ulcer, hyperinsulinism) are withheld because the component-tumor identities' own published windows carry them (ME-29).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia documents primary hyperparathyroidism as its most penetrant component at genetic-cohort and nationwide level: the Russian cohort of 102 genetically confirmed MEN1 patients from 43 families describes the classic triad of primary hyperparathyroidism, gastrointestinal neuroendocrine neoplasms, and pituitary adenomas and stratifies disease course by age at hyperparathyroidism onset (PMID 41834593), the South Korea nationwide cohort of 412 clinically suspected MEN1 cases found parathyroid involvement the most common manifestation at 58.6 percent (PMID 40607214), and the review of 14 studies covering 3,783 MEN2 or RET-variant carriers found MEN2-associated primary hyperparathyroidism prevalence between 7.84 and 31.3 percent with synchronous diagnosis alongside medullary thyroid carcinoma in 80 percent (PMID 40277809); the relationship is recorded as documented syndrome-component association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the MEN1 and MEN2 pathways differ in penetrance and mechanism (parathyroid multiglandular hyperplasia versus RET-driven adenoma), and the Korean cohort is ICD-defined clinically suspected disease rather than genetically confirmed, so any individual hyperparathyroidism claim requires germline confirmation and endocrine attribution with vitamin-D, renal, and familial-hypocalciuric exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Germline MEN1 loss of function or RET gain of function drives multigland parathyroid clonal proliferation so autonomous PTH secretion and primary hyperparathyroidism result, the tumor-predisposition route documented by the classic-triad framing and the nationwide parathyroid-involvement predominance, but whether this route produced any individual hyperparathyroidism remains hypothesized until germline and ionized-calcium records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at genetic-cohort plus nationwide-claims class only: the Russian cohort is 102 patients at one specialist center, the Korean cohort uses clinical-suspect operational definitions without genetic confirmation, and the MEN2 prevalence range (7.84-31.3 percent) spans heterogeneous screening intensities across 14 studies.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No single population-based penetrance figure exists across MEN1 and MEN2 combined; the syndromic types differ in mechanism and penetrance and are pooled only at the catalog-identity level; the Korean cohort's suspected-case definition may misclassify; normocalcemic and subclinical presentations alter ascertainment; and vitamin-D deficiency, thiazide use, and renal disease are competing hypercalcemia causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (benign mimicker of primary hyperparathyroidism)
vitamin-D deficiency and secondary hyperparathyroidism
thiazide and lithium effects on calcium
sporadic parathyroid adenoma in the general population
hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome and other familial forms

evidenceGaps: No single population-based penetrance figure exists across MEN1 and MEN2 combined; the syndromic types differ in mechanism and penetrance and are pooled only at the catalog-identity level; the Korean cohort's suspected-case definition may misclassify; normocalcemic and subclinical presentations alter ascertainment; and vitamin-D deficiency, thiazide use, and renal disease are competing hypercalcemia causes.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the tumor-predisposition precedent with the syndromic-heterogeneity limit carried openly: the Russian 102-patient MEN1 cohort describes the classic triad led by primary hyperparathyroidism (PMID 41834593), the South Korea nationwide cohort found parathyroid involvement the most common manifestation at 58.6 percent (PMID 40607214), and the 14-study MEN2 review found hyperparathyroidism prevalence 7.84-31.3 percent (PMID 40277809); because the syndromic types differ in mechanism and penetrance and the nationwide cohort is clinically suspected rather than genetically confirmed, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through germline confirmation and ionized-calcium workup with vitamin-D, renal, and familial-mimic exclusion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 documents pituitary adenoma development at nationwide cohort level: the nationwide multicenter retrospective cohort of 240 MEN1 patients found pituitary adenomas in 112 (46.6 percent) at mean age 36.1 years with most diagnosed through screening, prolactinomas (49.1 percent) and microadenomas (62.5 percent) predominating and prior primary hyperparathyroidism independently marking higher risk (HR 3.09) (PMID 40921719), the Russian 102-patient cohort records pituitary adenomas as the third element of the classic triad with exon 10 mutations carrying 7.7-fold increased pituitary adenoma risk (PMID 41834593), and the South Korea nationwide cohort found pituitary involvement in 22.3 percent of suspected MEN1 cases (PMID 40607214); the relationship is recorded as documented syndrome-component association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: pituitary adenoma prevalence estimates range from 22 to 47 percent across screening intensities and definitions, and MEN1 tumor predisposition does not determine which carriers develop adenomas, so any individual pituitary lesion claim requires germline and dedicated sellar imaging attribution with incidentaloma and medication exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Germline MEN1 loss of function drives anterior-pituitary clonal proliferation so pituitary adenoma results, the tumor-predisposition route consistent with the screening-detected predominance and the genotype-phenotype signal (exon 10 mutations with 7.7-fold adenoma risk), but whether this route produced any individual adenoma remains hypothesized until germline and sellar MRI records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at nationwide retrospective plus genetic-cohort class only: the 240-patient cohort is retrospective with 63.3 percent of adenomas screening-detected (ascertainment-dependent prevalence), the Russian cohort's genotype-phenotype signal is single-center with wide confidence bounds, and the Korean figure uses clinically suspected rather than genetically confirmed MEN1.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located study establishes penetrance by age in unselected MEN1 carriers prospectively; screening intensity drives detection; incidental pituitary microadenomas in the general population overlap the screening-detected burden; prolactinoma treatment (dopamine agonists) alters the natural history; and genotype-phenotype correlation remains unconfirmed beyond single-center signals.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: sporadic pituitary incidentaloma (common population finding)
prolactin elevation from medication or stalk effect
idiopathic hyperprolactinemia
other genetic pituitary syndromes (Carney complex, familial isolated pituitary adenoma)
hypopituitarism from treatment rather than tumor (the published hypopituitarism window)

evidenceGaps: No located study establishes penetrance by age in unselected MEN1 carriers prospectively; screening intensity drives detection; incidental pituitary microadenomas in the general population overlap the screening-detected burden; prolactinoma treatment (dopamine agonists) alters the natural history; and genotype-phenotype correlation remains unconfirmed beyond single-center signals.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the tumor-predisposition precedent with the ascertainment limit carried openly: the nationwide 240-patient MEN1 cohort found pituitary adenomas in 46.6 percent with screening predominance and prior hyperparathyroidism marking higher risk (PMID 40921719), the Russian cohort records the classic triad with exon 10 mutations carrying 7.7-fold adenoma risk (PMID 41834593), and the Korean nationwide cohort found pituitary involvement in 22.3 percent (PMID 40607214); because prevalence estimates span 22 to 47 percent across screening intensities and incidental microadenomas overlap the detected burden, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through germline confirmation and dedicated sellar imaging with incidentaloma and medication exclusion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 documents pheochromocytoma as its second main component at RET-genotype cohort level: the 309-patient MEN2 cohort found pheochromocytoma in 85 patients with RET-codon-specific penetrance (exon 11: 46.6 percent; exon 16: 41.2 percent; exon 10: 29.8 percent; exons 13-15: 1.7 percent) and age-related penetrance rising steadily (PMID 28605116), the MEN2 pheochromocytoma review reports variable penetrance from 10 to 80 percent depending on the RET mutation and calls pheochromocytoma the main disease to screen in RET carriers (PMID 32388798), and the de novo MEN2A case documented bilateral medullary thyroid carcinoma with a left pheochromocytoma (PMID 42272368); the relationship is recorded as documented syndrome-component association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: penetrance is RET-codon-specific and age-dependent with lifelong surveillance required, and the case anchor is a single de novo presentation, so any individual pheochromocytoma claim requires germline RET confirmation and biochemical screening with essential-hypertension, medication, and incidental-renal-mass exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Germline RET gain of function drives adrenomedullary chromaffin clonal proliferation so catecholamine-secreting pheochromocytoma results, the tumor-predisposition route documented by the codon-specific penetrance gradient and the screening framing, but whether this route produced any individual pheochromocytoma remains hypothesized until germline and plasma-metanephrine records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single-center 309-patient cohort plus narrative review class only: the penetrance figures come from one specialist ambulatory center spanning 1968-2015 with changing diagnostic methods (clinical to biochemical/imaging), the review's 10-80 percent range reflects mutation heterogeneity rather than population incidence, and malignant pheochromocytoma in MEN2 is recorded as rare.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No population-based incidence figure exists for MEN2 pheochromocytoma; penetrance estimates vary widely by RET codon and ascertainment; diagnostic methods changed across the four decades of the anchor cohort; variable expressivity within families is documented; and essential hypertension and incidentally discovered adrenal adenomas compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: sporadic adrenal incidentaloma
essential hypertension with elevated catecholamines from stress or medication
other hereditary pheochromocytoma syndromes (VHL, SDHx, NF1)
adrenal cortical adenoma
anxiety and panic physiology mimicking catecholamine excess

evidenceGaps: No population-based incidence figure exists for MEN2 pheochromocytoma; penetrance estimates vary widely by RET codon and ascertainment; diagnostic methods changed across the four decades of the anchor cohort; variable expressivity within families is documented; and essential hypertension and incidentally discovered adrenal adenomas compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the tumor-predisposition precedent with the codon-specific-penetrance limit carried openly: the 309-patient MEN2 cohort found pheochromocytoma in 85 patients with RET-codon-specific penetrance from 1.7 to 46.6 percent and steadily age-rising risk (PMID 28605116), the MEN2 review reports penetrance 10-80 percent by RET mutation (PMID 32388798), and the de novo MEN2A case documented pheochromocytoma alongside bilateral medullary thyroid carcinoma (PMID 42272368); because penetrance is codon-specific and age-dependent and the anchor cohort spans changing diagnostic eras, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through germline RET confirmation and biochemical screening with hypertension, medication, and incidental-mass exclusion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 documents medullary thyroid carcinoma as its core malignant component at genotype-cohort and family-study level: the 309-patient MEN2 cohort records medullary thyroid carcinoma diagnosed synchronously or metachronously with pheochromocytoma and finds pheochromocytoma penetrance correlated with medullary thyroid carcinoma aggressiveness based on RET mutation status (PMID 28605116), the RET K666N family study documents familial medullary thyroid carcinoma with bilateral subcentimeter foci and C-cell hyperplasia across three generations (PMID 39963300), and the de novo MEN2A case presented with bilateral medullary thyroid carcinoma as the revealing manifestation (PMID 42272368); the relationship is recorded as documented syndrome-component association only, scoped to the medullary histotype.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the medullary histotype is a specific C-cell carcinoma rather than generic thyroid carcinoma, RET codon status determines aggressiveness and timing, and the family anchors are case class, so any individual thyroid malignancy claim requires germline RET and calcitonin/histologic attribution with follicular-variant and incidental-nodule exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Germline RET gain of function drives parafollicular C-cell clonal progression through C-cell hyperplasia so medullary thyroid carcinoma results, the documented precursor sequence in the family study and the genotype-aggressiveness correlation in the cohort, but whether this route produced any individual carcinoma remains hypothesized until germline, calcitonin, and histopathologic records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single-center genotype cohort plus family case class only: the 309-patient cohort spans 1968-2015 with changing diagnostic methods, the family study is one kindred with a rare low-penetrance RET variant (K666N), and no located material quantifies medullary carcinoma incidence in generic thyroid-cancer terms because the catalog lacks a medullary-specific identity.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located study reports medullary carcinoma incidence under the generic thyroid-cancer identity definition; the catalog lacks a medullary-thyroid-carcinoma identity so the edge is scoped to the medullary histotype only; the K666N family shows age-dependent expressivity with low penetrance of other MEN2 tumors; RET codon status drives wide aggressiveness variation; and sporadic medullary carcinoma (non-germline) and follicular-derived thyroid nodules compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma without RET germline variant
follicular-derived thyroid neoplasms (the published nontoxic-thyroid-enlargement and thyroiditis scopes)
C-cell hyperplasia without carcinoma
benign thyroid nodules and incidentalomas
other RET-associated phenotypes without thyroid malignancy

evidenceGaps: No located study reports medullary carcinoma incidence under the generic thyroid-cancer identity definition; the catalog lacks a medullary-thyroid-carcinoma identity so the edge is scoped to the medullary histotype only; the K666N family shows age-dependent expressivity with low penetrance of other MEN2 tumors; RET codon status drives wide aggressiveness variation; and sporadic medullary carcinoma (non-germline) and follicular-derived thyroid nodules compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the tumor-predisposition precedent with the histotype-scope limit carried openly: the 309-patient MEN2 cohort links RET mutation status to medullary thyroid carcinoma aggressiveness with synchronous or metachronous pheochromocytoma (PMID 28605116), the RET K666N family documents familial medullary carcinoma with C-cell hyperplasia (PMID 39963300), and the de novo MEN2A case presented with bilateral medullary carcinoma (PMID 42272368); because the catalog lacks a medullary-specific identity and the family anchors are case class with codon-dependent penetrance, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, scopes it explicitly to the medullary histotype, and routes individual claims through germline RET and calcitonin/histologic confirmation with follicular-variant and incidental-nodule exclusion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 documents gastrinoma as its most frequent functional pancreaticoduodenal tumor at surgical-cohort and case level: the AFCE-GTE study of 31 MEN1 patients undergoing pancreatoduodenectomy for duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors lists Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (gastrinoma) as the surgical indication in 18 (58 percent) and reports biochemical cure for MEN1-related gastrinomas in about 60 percent (PMID 33649917), the MEN1 pregnancy case documented biochemically proven primary hyperparathyroidism with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome evidence on endoscopy (PMID 33597314), and the Russian 102-patient cohort records gastrointestinal neuroendocrine neoplasms as the second element of the MEN1 classic triad (PMID 41834593); the relationship is recorded as documented syndrome-component association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the surgical cohort is conditioned on operative selection for large or functioning tumors and the case anchor is a single pregnancy presentation, so any individual gastrinoma claim requires germline MEN1 confirmation and gastrin/secretin-stimulated attribution with proton-pump-inhibitor and antral-G-cell exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Germline MEN1 loss of function drives duodenal gastrin-cell clonal proliferation so gastrinoma with autonomous gastrin secretion results, the tumor-predisposition route consistent with gastrinoma predominance among functioning duodenopancreatic tumors in the MEN1 surgical cohort and the triad's gastrointestinal neuroendocrine component, but whether this route produced any individual gastrinoma remains hypothesized until germline and gastrin-stimulation records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at surgical-cohort plus case class only: the 31-patient cohort is conditioned on pancreatoduodenectomy selection, the pregnancy case is a single observation, and no located population cohort reports gastrinoma incidence in MEN1 carriers under modern screening.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located population-based penetrance figure for gastrinoma in MEN1; surgical series are selection-conditioned; proton-pump-inhibitor therapy blunts gastrin assays and alters presentation; duodenal versus pancreatic primary sites carry different prognoses unmodeled here; and sporadic duodenal gastrinoma and antral G-cell hyperplasia compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: sporadic duodenal or pancreatic gastrinoma without MEN1
antral G-cell hyperplasia and hypergastrinemia from PPI therapy
gastric outlet and renal hypergastrinemia
peptic ulcer disease from other causes (the published peptic-ulcer-disease window; its gastrinoma pathway is not recycled per ME-29)
other MEN1 pancreaticoduodenal tumors (insulinoma on the companion edge)

evidenceGaps: No located population-based penetrance figure for gastrinoma in MEN1; surgical series are selection-conditioned; proton-pump-inhibitor therapy blunts gastrin assays and alters presentation; duodenal versus pancreatic primary sites carry different prognoses unmodeled here; and sporadic duodenal gastrinoma and antral G-cell hyperplasia compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the tumor-predisposition precedent with the surgical-selection limit carried openly: the AFCE-GTE cohort of 31 MEN1 patients found Zollinger-Ellison syndrome the indication in 58 percent of pancreatoduodenectomies for duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with biochemical cure in about 60 percent of MEN1-related gastrinomas (PMID 33649917), the MEN1 pregnancy case documented Zollinger-Ellison syndrome alongside primary hyperparathyroidism (PMID 33597314), and the Russian cohort records the gastrointestinal neuroendocrine component of the classic triad (PMID 41834593); because the surgical cohort is selection-conditioned and no population penetrance figure exists, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through germline MEN1 confirmation and gastrin-stimulation testing with PPI and antral exclusion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 documents insulinoma at international surgical-cohort level: the 46-center international cohort of 96 MEN1-related insulinoma resections states that insulinomas are found in 10-15 percent of MEN1 patients and lead to life-threatening hypoglycaemia, with multifocal disease in 33 of 96 and recurrent or new insulinoma during follow-up (PMID 32352164), the AFCE-GTE pancreatoduodenectomy cohort lists insulinoma as the surgical indication in 2 of 31 MEN1 patients (7 percent) (PMID 33649917), and the South Korea nationwide cohort recorded duodenopancreatic tumors in 19.9 percent of clinically suspected MEN1 cases (PMID 40607214); the relationship is recorded as documented syndrome-component association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the 10-15 percent figure is drawn from surgical and specialist series conditioned on symptomatic presentation, and multifocal pancreatic neuroendocrine disease complicates lesion-level attribution, so any individual insulinoma claim requires germline MEN1 confirmation and supervised fasting/insulin-proinsulin attribution with factitious and sulfonylurea exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Germline MEN1 loss of function drives pancreatic beta-cell clonal proliferation so insulinoma with autonomous insulin secretion and hypoglycaemia results, the tumor-predisposition route consistent with the 10-15 percent frequency in MEN1 and the multifocal disease pattern in the international cohort, but whether this route produced any individual insulinoma remains hypothesized until germline and supervised-fast records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at international surgical cohort plus specialist-review class only: the 96-patient cohort is conditioned on operative referral across 46 centers over 26 years, the 10-15 percent frequency is a specialist estimate rather than a population penetrance figure, and the surgical-comparison cohort contains only 2 insulinoma indications.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No population-based penetrance figure for insulinoma in MEN1; symptomatic ascertainment enriches severe presentations; multifocal pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors make lesion-level diagnosis difficult; metachronous new insulinomas occur in multifocal disease; and factitious hypoglycaemia, sulfonylureas, and non-insulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglycaemia compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: sporadic pancreatic insulinoma without MEN1
factitious hypoglycaemia and sulfonylurea use
nesidioblastosis and non-insulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglycaemia
adrenal insufficiency and hepatic hypoglycaemia (the published addisons-disease window)
other MEN1 pancreaticoduodenal tumors (gastrinoma on the companion edge)
